title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control.
significance: While laboratory BCIs have decoded speech and cursor control with impressive accuracy, they have required constant technical supervision and lab environments, blocking real clinical translation. This work demonstrates that an intracortical BCI system can be operated independently by a patient at home for extended periods, supporting both naturalistic speech decoding and digital cursor control without expert oversight. This is a landmark proof of concept that addresses the critical gap between research prototypes and practical, patient-independent neurotechnology, showing that implantable BCIs can deliver genuine functional benefit and usability in real life, not just in controlled settings.

title: Neuropixels Opto: combining high-resolution electrophysiology and optogenetics.
significance: This paper enables simultaneous high-resolution recording and spatially precise optogenetic manipulation of thousands of neurons, revolutionizing circuit neuroscience research capabilities.

title: Deep brain stimulation induces white matter remodeling and functional changes to brain-wide networks.
significance: This study reveals how DBS mechanically remodels white matter and reorganizes brain networks, providing crucial biological mechanisms explaining why this treatment alleviates depression.

title: Responsive stimulation of the thalamus for idiopathic generalized epilepsy: Results of the randomized controlled NAUTILUS trial through 18 months.
significance: This trial demonstrates that responsive thalamic stimulation safely reduces seizures in drug-resistant generalized epilepsy patients who lack other effective treatment options.

title: Frequency-dependent cerebellar circuits independently gate social vocalizations and movement.
Simultaneous speech and gesture decoding for multimodal communication in paralysis.
significance: This landmark result demonstrates that a single implanted electrode array can decode both speech and gesture intentions from the same neural population, opening the door to naturalistic two-channel communication for people with severe paralysis. By showing that these modalities can be separated and recombined in real time, it represents a major advance in the practical utility and bandwidth of BCI systems. This multimodal approach substantially improves what severely disabled users can express compared to single-modality BCIs, moving the field toward genuine conversational interfaces.

title: Effective stimulation sites and networks for substantia nigra pars reticulata deep brain stimulation for auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia.
significance: This work applies deep brain stimulation to a new psychiatric target (substantia nigra pars reticulata) for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, with acute outcome mapping using connectomics. It represents a clinically meaningful advance in understanding how DBS engages distributed brain networks to suppress symptoms, bridging device implantation with mechanistic circuit analysis. This directional progress in DBS applications and targeting refinement matters to practitioners developing psychiatric neuromodulation protocols.

title: Inhibiting the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex selectively enhances unsupervised statistical learning.
Is It Safe to Have Deep Brain Stimulation after MRI-Guided Focused Ultrasound Ablation? A Report of Three Cases and Review of Literature.
significance: This work explores a practical compatibility question between two distinct neuromodulation platforms: focused ultrasound ablation and deep brain stimulation. When tremor recurs after MRgFUS treatment, clinicians may consider adding DBS, raising safety concerns about hardware interactions, imaging compatibility, and device function. The report contributes incremental but clinically important knowledge about how multiple implanted neurotechnologies can coexist safely and function together in patients.

title: Optimal positioning and size of high-density electrocorticography grids for speech brain-computer interfaces.
significance: This work directly optimizes the physical design of implanted ECoG electrode arrays for speech decoding, focusing on where grids should be positioned and how many electrodes are necessary to maximize word classification while keeping surgery practical. These are core neurotechnology engineering problems that determine feasibility and performance of implantable speech BCIs. The findings inform surgical planning and hardware specifications for future clinical deployments.

title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex modulates single-neuron activity in humans.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
significance: This work uses simultaneous intracranial microelectrode recording and transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in neurosurgical patients to reveal how cortical stimulation alters activity in individual neurons within mood-regulating circuits. TMS is an established clinical neuromodulation technology, and understanding its mechanism at the single-neuron level validates its efficacy and could guide optimization of stimulation parameters. The finding strengthens the scientific foundation for TMS as a neurotechnology platform.

title: Closed-loop transcranial electrical brain stimulation with fMRI: A proof-of-concept randomized trial of real-time fMRI-guided tACS optimization.
significance: This randomized trial demonstrates one of the first closed-loop systems combining transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS) with real-time functional MRI feedback to automatically adjust stimulation parameters based on ongoing brain activity. This is core neurotechnology work because it builds an adaptive neuromodulation system that uses neural monitoring to optimize delivery in real time. Closed-loop systems that respond to brain state represent a major frontier in noninvasive neuromodulation, making this a significant methodological and clinical advance for the field.
